source: Condensed from docs/decoders.md in the ECCentric repository (https://github.com/TUM-DSE/eccentric/blob/main/docs/decoders.md). Edit here when that file changes; the statistics on the Decoders page are computed from data/sweep.json and figures/decoders.csv by tools/build.py.

decoders.description: Google's most-likely-error search decoder, run with its default configuration. The most accurate decoder in the benchmark, but slow beyond a few hundred qubits; used as the accuracy reference.

Two-pass correlated matching with PyMatching, as in Cain et al. (2024): the first pass reweights the second. Errors that Stim cannot decompose into matching edges are split by matching their own detectors.
decoders.applies: Matchable codes, including circuits whose errors do not decompose into edges

decoders.description: Minimum-weight perfect matching (PyMatching) on the error model decomposed into edges. Microseconds per shot. It refuses circuits whose errors do not decompose into edges, which includes some routed heavy-hex, honeycomb and surface circuits.
decoders.applies: Matchable codes: surface, heavy-hex, Bacon-Shor, repetition, XZZX, toric, honeycomb, hyperbolic Floquet

decoders.description: IBM's Relay-BP with the paper's parameters: chains of BP runs with memory, built for bivariate bicycle codes. Run on the exact syndromes (relay-bp 0.2.1 pads them through its sinter interface).

The same BP-OSD with tuned BP: 100 iterations, min-sum scaling 0.625. In a pilot it gave 20% lower logical error rates on topological and other low-weight codes at a tenth of the time, but up to 3× higher on some qLDPC codes, so the sweep runs it next to BP-OSD on the former.
Belief propagation followed by ordered-statistics decoding (ldpc). The usual choice for qLDPC codes, and the general decoder of the paper.
Belief propagation followed by localised statistics decoding (ldpc), with the same BP settings as BP-OSD.
Belief propagation followed by union-find (ldpc), with the same BP settings as BP-OSD.

Normalized min-sum on the GARI-transformed correlated error model, with the authors' C decoder (vendored) in their standalone setting: 400 iterations, normalization 0.96875. Checked against their published results. A shot it does not converge on gets no correction.
decoders.applies: CSS memory circuits; not applicable where detectors or errors lack the X/Z structure it needs

decoders.description: Beta reimplementation (the authors have not released theirs): GARI for at most 7 iterations, then union-find on the residual syndrome, guided by GARI's posteriors. The paper uses Chromobius and its own hypergraph union-find as second stages; this uses ldpc's union-find everywhere.
The Möbius decoder for color codes: matching on a doubled graph, using the color and basis annotations of the color code's detectors.
Hypergraph minimum-weight parity factor, with cluster_node_limit = 50 as in its README. Matches on the undecomposed error model, so it also decodes circuits where MWPM fails.
Level-by-level decoding of concatenated codes (Poulin, 2006): BP level by level, each level's posteriors as the next level's priors, then BP-OSD on all detectors.
decoders.applies: Concatenated codes: many-hypercube, concatenated Steane at d = 9 and 27

decoders.description: As level-by-level BP-OSD, but each level passes hard decisions instead of posteriors to the next.
Weighted union-find (ldpc). Fast on topological codes; fails on qLDPC codes.
Belief propagation followed by matching with the BP marginals as edge weights.
